title: POC scoping: private networking & data residency - HelixCare
summary: POC scoping for private networking and data residency. Customer needs VPC-only connectivity (no egress to public internet), EU data residency for PHI-lite workloads, and clear success criteria for latency, throughput, and security controls. Discussed options: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, dedicated capacity, KMS integration, and a 6-week POC plan with benchmarks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (HelixCare CTO), Ethan Ruiz (HelixCare DevOps), Priya Nambiar (HelixCare Security)

Summary (auto): quick scoping call on private networking and data residency. Focus on networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), zero-egress requirements, EU residency, sizing, and POC timeline.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. With me is Samir, our SE.
[00:08] Samir Patel: hi all, Samir here. we'll go over network patterns then sizing and benchmarks.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: great, thanks. quick context: HelixCare builds a patient-facing triage assistant. Not full PHI but potentially sensitive, we prefer EU residency for european customers and strict egress rules. timeline: interested in a POC in April, target production Q3.
[00:28] Ethan Ruiz: yep infra notes: we run core services in eu-west-1, have a transit gateway and strict egress policies - basically no outbound internet from subnets that touch PHI-adjacent workloads.
[00:40] Priya Nambiar: security: SOC 2 ok, need KMS ownership, audit logs sent to our SIEM, SAML SSO, RBAC. also need to understand persistence and logging on Redwood side - do logs ever leave our account?
[01:00] Lena: good constraints. high-level options: hosted with PrivateLink (AWS VPC Endpoint Service) or Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (private deployment) - both can avoid public internet. For Dedicated we can support private control plane or customer-managed control plane depending on the package.
[01:20] Samir: demoing the networking: VPC peering is straightforward but cross-account peering can have routing complexities; PrivateLink (AWS NLB+EndpointService) gives simpler, managed private connectivity and avoids route table exposure. Transit Gateway is another pattern for multi-VPC setups.
[01:45] Maya: what's the tradeoff for PrivateLink vs peering?
[01:50] Samir: peering gives direct L3 connectivity, lower latency, but you need to manage routes and propagate prefixes; can be hairy if you have many VPCs. PrivateLink uses elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in your VPC and traffic stays private, but there can be small NAT-like behavior for DNS and the throughput per ENI is finite; we usually recommend PrivateLink for single-VPC or app-facing endpoints, peering or Transit Gateway for internal network topologies.
[02:15] Ethan: any IP ranges or CIDR requirements? we want to avoid overlapping ranges.
[02:19] Samir: we'll need a non-overlapping CIDR for the peering side, or PrivateLink endpoints in your VPC which don't require peering but do require security group/open ports to the endpoint. We'll include a networking checklist with exact CIDR and SG rules.
[02:35] Priya: KMS - can we bring our own key?
[02:38] Lena: yes, for Dedicated/Private deployments we support BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS/HSM integrations) so keys and encrypted artifacts remain under your control. For hosted we support envelope encryption with your KMS in some enterprise plans - we'll confirm the exact model in the security pack.
[02:58] Maya: data residency: we need EU-only processing for EU customers. Can you guarantee no tokenization or replication to US regions?
[03:06] Samir: yes, with private deployment we can pin model hosting to eu regions only. For hosted we have region selection and can route to eu clusters, but we need to ensure logs/metrics and backups also stay in-region - that's part of the POC scope. We'll map all data flows.
[03:30] Lena: success criteria we discussed include: p95 latency under 200ms for short-turn prompts (seq len ~256), sustained 50 QPS for typical inference endpoint, no egress to public internet, KMS BYOK in place, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. If we hit those in the POC and your integration tests pass, we consider POC successful.
[03:55] Ethan: are those realistic? 50 QPS @ 256 seq - what hardware are we talking about?
[03:59] Samir: depends on model. For a 7B-ish conversational model on quantized H100 or multi-A100 setup we can hit 50 QPS with batching and KV cache, but exacts depend on batch sizes and prompt distribution. We'll need sample payloads. We'll propose two benchmark targets: baseline (no KV cache, conservative) and optimized (with cache, batching). p99 targets will be higher, we'll capture p95/p99.
[04:30] Maya: would you recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private?
[04:34] Lena: for your constraints (no egress, EU residency, KMS BYOK) Dedicated in your VPC or Private deployment is safest. Hosted with PrivateLink can work but we'd need additional contracts for log residency and possibly dedicated capacity to guarantee isolation.
[04:50] Priya: audit logs - can we have them stream to an S3 bucket in our account?
[04:55] Samir: yes for Dedicated/Private we can forward audit logs to your S3 and CloudWatch in your account. Hosted options may require log forwarding with push to your endpoint - we'll detail in the security bundle.
[05:12] Lena: ok let's talk timeline - a proposed 6-week POC:
[05:17] Samir: week 0 (network prep) - exchange networking details, set up PrivateLink or peering, KMS policy. Week 1 - model onboarding and baseline benchmarks. Week 2 - integration tests, sample traffic. Week 3 - optimize batching/cache and run sustained load tests. Week 4 - run production-like regression tests and failover. Week 5 - security/attestation checks and docs. Week 6 - handoff and SOW finalization.
[05:44] Ethan: that sounds fine, but we need a faster initial smoke test in week 1 to unblock product.
[05:48] Samir: we can do a 48-72 hour smoke test once networking is in place. baseline latency and functional checks.
[05:55] Maya: for benchmarks - what metrics will you collect?
[05:58] Samir: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, tokens per request, CPU/GPU utilization, GPU memory, KV cache hit rates, end-to-end request time including network RTT. We'll provide a spreadsheet for you to fill sample payloads and desired QPS.
[06:15] Priya: regarding egress - we need to know if any calls to external telemetry or license checks egress to third-party.
[06:21] Lena: good callout. We'll list all external endpoints used by Redwood. For Dedicated/Private, there are minimal control-plane calls; many can be routed through your control plane. We'll document telemetry and allow opt-out where possible.
[06:38] Ethan: what about DNS resolution for PrivateLink? we use internal DNS, do you support that?
[06:42] Samir: yes, PrivateLink will create ENI-facing DNS names; you can control via Route53 private hosted zones. We also support explicit IP-based routing for peering. We'll include DNS playbook.
[06:58] Maya: costs - if we go Dedicated, what is the expected cost runway for a pilot?
[07:03] Lena: we'll send pricing ranges. Typical small pilot reserved capacity for a 6-week POC is a few thousand dollars to tens of thousands depending on GPU type (A100/H100) and throughput targets. We'll provide a model and a per-token estimate in the worksheet.
[07:20] Ethan: any pre-networking requirements from our side? firewall rules, SGs?
[07:24] Samir: yes we'll need outbound to the PrivateLink endpoint and specific ports for gRPC/HTTPS depending on the endpoint. We'll include a checklist: SGs, NACLs, IPs, DNS, IAM roles for KMS access.
[07:40] Maya: if we need on-prem later, does Redwood support air-gapped?
[07:44] Lena: yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem packages, but that's a bigger engagement. For this POC we'll focus on VPC-based Dedicated.
[07:55] Ethan: sample payloads - one question: average tokens per request is ~120 after context, with some bursts up to 1024 for long threads. is that ok?
[08:03] Samir: yes we can model that. Bursty long sequences change batching tradeoffs; we'll include a few workload profiles: short chat (120 tokens), medium (256), long (512+).
[08:15] Lena: any blockers for starting week of April 6th?
[08:18] Maya: we can start networking the week of April 6th if you can get the checklist and the SOW draft this week.
[08:24] Priya: we also need to review the KMS policy sample and the data flows.
[08:27] Lena: will do.
[08:30] Samir: i'll outline the benchmark harness we'll use - JMeter/gRPC client and our tracing hooks - so you can run in your environment as well.
[08:40] Ethan: for the smoke test - what endpoints do we hit and auth?
[08:43] Samir: token-based auth tied to your account, and for PrivateLink we'll use mutual TLS or signed tokens depending on the setup. We'll include sample curl commands and a small SDK snippet.
[08:55] Maya: ok good. any competitor concerns? we've seen Anthropic's private options and Bedrock marketplace - how are you different?
[09:03] Lena: Redwood differentiates on serving runtime/production controls and observability - batching, KV cache, smart routing, and transparent performance profiles. we'll show you p95/p99 tradeoffs and cost levers in the workshop.
[09:18] Priya: can you sign a DPA with EU data residency clauses?
[09:22] Lena: yes, we have templates and can add clauses - legal will help finalize. we'll surface typical language in the SOW and DPA.
[09:32] Ethan: anything else on networking?
[09:34] Samir: one more note - if you use AWS PrivateLink with LZ (Landing Zone) and multiple accounts we might need to coordinate endpoint sharing. We'll capture that as a requirement in the checklist.
[09:48] Maya: recap - deliverables from Redwood: networking checklist, security pack (SOC2, KMS BYOK instructions), sizing worksheet, benchmark plan, pricing and SOW draft. From us: payloads, QPS targets, preferred regions, KMS policy and SIEM endpoint.
[10:05] Lena: yes. we'll follow up with those docs and propose a follow-up meeting to kick off the network setup.
[10:12] Maya: thanks all.

Notes & minor transcription artifacts: sometimes "PrivateLink" was written as "Private Link"; "KV cache" occasionally transcribed as "K V cache"; "Redwood" was transcribed as "redwwod" in one place.

End of call.
